newsitem.title: ITALY: Federmeccanica says has support of Italy industry.
newsitem.headline: Federmeccanica says has support of Italy industry.

text.p: The chairman of Italy's engineering and metalworking industry employers' federation said on Thursday he had the full support of other industrialists for the group's stance in its dispute with trades unions over pay.
The group, Federmeccanica, has rejected a government proposal to award workers a 200,000 lire ($129) a month pay rise to cover the 1996-98 contract period.

Unions in the sector have asked for talks on the dispute to be conducted at the level of government, the three main labour confederations and the industrialists' umbrella body Confindustria, rather than at the industry level.

"Within Confindustria I did not expect such a level of support for our line. It is almost embarrassing," Federmeccanica chairman Gabriele Albertini told reporters after a regular Confindustria meeting.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu was expected to meet the parties in this dispute this week.

Unions have been locked in dispute with employers since last July over the renewal of contracts in the sector and said on Wednesday they would hold 10 hours of strikes on a factory-by-factory basis between now and January 25.

The unions, which had been seeking a 230,000 lire increase, have accepted the government proposal but management is unwilling to pay out more than 139,000 lire a month unless the government offers companies big incentives in compensation.
